questions.q: Tell me about the accounts work you did in your last job or internship. What entries, reports or tasks were yours?
questions.looks_for: Names concrete tasks (vouchers, ledgers, bank reconciliation, payables, receivables, GST data), the business type and software, and their own share of the work.

questions.q: Describe a time you found a mistake or mismatch in the books. How did you find it and how was it fixed?
questions.looks_for: A specific mismatch (bank vs books, wrong ledger, duplicate entry), how they traced it, the correction entry, and what was done to avoid it again.

questions.q: What is a bank reconciliation, and why can the bank balance and the book balance be different on the same day?
questions.looks_for: Matching bank statement with cash book; reasons like cheques issued not cleared, deposits not credited, bank charges or interest not yet entered.

questions.q: Can you explain the difference between an expense and an asset, with an example from a small business?
questions.looks_for: Expense is used up in the period (rent, salary); asset gives benefit over time (computer, vehicle) and is depreciated; shows why the difference changes profit.

questions.q: What is accrual accounting, and how would you record an electricity bill for March that is paid in April?
questions.looks_for: Record income and expenses when they happen, not when cash moves; book March expense with a payable (outstanding) in March, then clear it on payment in April.

questions.q: At month end your manager asks for the closing figures today, but two vendor bills are missing and one payment entry looks doubtful. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Follows up with vendors or purchase team, books known items, clearly flags missing and doubtful items instead of guessing, informs the manager with a list, does not fudge figures.

questions.q: Why do you want this accounts executive job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
